entries.title: AI-Assisted SharePoint Knowledge Workbench Research (index)
entries.content_summary: Directory index and vision statement for docs/research/. Describes the layered capability model (SharePoint agents, native Copilot skills, Cowork, Copilot Studio, GitHub Copilot workbench), lists all research documents with reading paths, records key findings and near-term priorities, and states repository conventions recommended by the research.
source_relationships: links to all 15 other docs/research/*.md files
inbound_references: docs/vision/README.md (line: 'docs/research/    product research and field notes')
entries.classification_rationale: Navigational index; content is the directory's own table of contents plus a synthesized 'key findings' section that itself has independent value and may need to survive any reorganization in some form.
entries.ambiguity: If docs/research/ is reorganized by subject domain, this index's list-by-reading-path structure will need to be rebuilt as a cross-domain index rather than a single flat list. Whether that becomes docs/research/README.md, docs/research/INDEX.md, or is distributed into per-domain READMEs is an architecture decision, not resolved here.

entries.title: Research Summary — Get Started with Copilot in SharePoint (Preview)
entries.content_summary: Summarizes Microsoft Learn's documented Copilot in SharePoint preview (as of June 25, 2026): natural-language interface for SharePoint content/structures, skills as an extension mechanism (Markdown SKILL.md in Agent Assets library), government-cloud limitation, licensing prerequisites, administrative controls, usage limits, and permission boundaries. Explicitly positions itself as research/architecture input, not implementation authorization.
overlaps_with: sharepoint-agents-and-native-skills-as-workbench-outputs.md (shares Microsoft-source citations on Copilot in SharePoint skills)
inbound_references: not yet grepped with line numbers; docs/research/README.md links to it
entries.classification_rationale: Pure external-source research summary with explicit publisher, URL, and source-updated date (June 25, 2026); no tenant testing; foundational for understanding platform licensing/preview constraints.

entries.title: Research Summary — Native Markdown Support in SharePoint and OneDrive
entries.content_summary: Summarizes Microsoft's April 21, 2026 announcement of native Markdown support in SharePoint/OneDrive: browser viewing, editing, versioning, governance implications, and explicit framing of Markdown as relevant to AI/agent shared team memory and reusable skills. Notes this strengthens but does not resolve source-of-truth/synchronization/approval architecture questions.
inbound_references: not yet grepped with line numbers
entries.classification_rationale: External product-announcement research directly relevant to Markdown-as-publication-target strategy.

entries.title: Research Summary — AI in SharePoint: From Content Chaos to Clarity and Impact
entries.content_summary: Summarizes a Microsoft 365 Community Conference 2026 presentation (Setup/Automate/Insight model for AI in SharePoint). Connects the three-part model to the workbench vision and lists government-specific controls the workbench vision adds beyond the product demo (ownership, approval, least-privilege, records/retention, accessibility, audit, rollback, oversharing protection).
entries.classification_rationale: High-level vision-supporting research; the government-controls list duplicates similar lists elsewhere in docs/research/README.md and docs/vision/ — a candidate for de-duplication review, not decided here.
entries.ambiguity: This document's government-controls list closely echoes docs/research/README.md's 'Government-Specific Controls' section. Whether that is intentional restatement or should be a single canonical list is an open question for architecture review.

entries.title: Research Summary — SharePoint Showcase: AI-Forward Content Creation and Curation
entries.content_summary: Summarizes a Microsoft SharePoint Blog / M365 Community Conference 2026 post on AI-assisted page creation/editing and continuous curation. Frames CREATION and CURATION as one lifecycle; connects content quality/freshness directly to Copilot/agent grounding quality.
entries.classification_rationale: Curation/creation lifecycle research; maps most directly to knowledge-curation concerns rather than pure platform capability.
entries.ambiguity: Could equally sit under sharepoint-platforms-capabilities (it's about a SharePoint product feature) or knowledge-discovery-retrieval (it's about curation/quality). Domain boundary is not sharp for this file.

Internally authored synthesis, not a single external-source summary.

entries.title: Field Note — Creating a Native SharePoint Skill in the AgentAssets Library

entries.title: Field Note — Ready-Made Copilot 'Launching' a Named Custom Agent (Confirmed Not a Real Hand-Off)
entries.content_summary: Records a CONFIRMED (not merely observed) finding from Phase 5 Task 4 manual verification: the 'launch by name' behavior is a UI/phrasing artifact, not a genuine agent hand-off. Supersedes/updates the original unverified observation referenced in prior discovery passes.
entries.classification_rationale: CORRECTION FROM PRIOR PASS: earlier discovery session (commit d618687) classified this as 'Research/Unverified' status with confidence=medium, citing an 'unverified observation requiring verification.' Actual document content shows the verification was already performed and the finding CONFIRMED on 2026-08-02. Prior classification was based on an out-of-date secondhand description (docs/research/README.md's summary of this file used cautious language), not the file's own current status line. This is exactly the failure mode the corpus-first process is meant to prevent.

entries.title: Field Note — .aspx vs. Rendered-Markdown Grounding: Live Comparison Findings
entries.content_summary: Tenant-tested evidence (7 cases, 1-2 runs each, 20 total live runs) comparing two live SharePoint Copilot agents grounded on identical content in ASPX vs. Markdown representations. Three findings: (1) both agents use upload-timestamp as a currency proxy — a general trust-boundary risk; (2) repeated runs of relationship questions can produce mutually contradictory confident answers; (3) one single-case ambiguity-handling difference favoring Markdown, not yet confirmed at scale. Explicitly extracted from the fuller Phase 5 evidence record for cross-phase relevance.
dependencies: full evidence record lives in tools/phase-5-sharepoint-knowledge-agent-pilot/results/task8-consolidated-findings.md — this file is explicitly a generalizable extract, not the complete record
entries.classification_rationale: High-value, well-evidenced field note with explicit confidence framing and multiple citing documents; the extraction relationship to the full Phase 5 evidence record must be preserved (link, not duplicate).
entries.ambiguity: This file already IS a synthesis/extraction of a fuller phase evidence record. A 'markdown-vs-aspx' consolidation group was hypothesized in the prior (incomplete) discovery pass, expecting a matching Phase 7 source — that Phase 7 source has not yet been located or confirmed to exist. Do not assume it exists; verify in next pass.
